video.title: Everyone Overlooks This Simple Side Hustle

summary: Chris Koerner interviews Don, who runs a family fresh-squeezed lemonade business at the Frisco and Dallas farmers markets in Texas. It made about $250k last year over about 8 months, selling 32oz cups at $7 that cost about $1.25 to make. Don explains the recipe, equipment (about $1,500 to start), warehouse prep, staffing with his kids, a $300 booth fee, and expansion into $1,000-3,000 caterings, $500 cart rentals via Facebook Marketplace, venue concessions and a $19k frozen-banana trade-show job. His advice is to stop overthinking and just post up with a quality fresh product.

tactics.name: Theatrical fresh-squeeze process
steps: Wedge the lemon with a Sunkist wedger
Smash with a pneumatic smasher customers can hear
Add 3oz 1:1 simple syrup, ~1lb ice, filtered water and shake
Squeeze a lemon in front of sceptics to prove freshness

quote.text: you can hear it like in our markets, you can hear it and you walk in, you hear the sounds like money
quote.speaker: Don

tactics.name: Batch prep at warehouse
steps: Buy 140-count lemons and 50lb sugar bags from Restaurant Depot / Ben E. Keith
Make 60-70 gallons of 1:1 simple syrup at a time by volume

tactics.name: Anchor price
steps: Set a value price ($7 for 32oz) and never move it

tactics.name: Upsell rentals with product
steps: List cart rental on Facebook Marketplace at $500
Suggest adding lemonade to the rental

tactics.name: Ask 'what else?' on catering leads
steps: When a client asks what else you do, offer a novel item (frozen bananas)
Freeze leftovers and sell at the next event

tactics.name: Multi-market staffing
steps: Owner drops trailer Friday night and restocks Sunday

lessons.lesson: Overlooked 'kid' businesses can be very lucrative because people think they're too good for them.

quote.text: people overlook it like I'm I'm too good for that
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Stop overthinking setup (LLC etc.); get a table, a tent and a recipe and post up.

quote.text: get a table, get a tent. Yeah. You know, like get your recipe right. Yeah. And then just post up
quote.speaker: Don

lessons.lesson: Authenticity (real fresh product) beats gimmicky competitors and removes competition worry.
Theatre and sound at the stall attract crowds.
Events and catering have much higher ticket sizes than walk-up sales.
A family business with kids involved looks wholesome and helps the brand.
Simple products are easier to sell walk-up; novel ones need explaining.

quote.text: Lemonade's easy. You have to explain bananas
quote.speaker: Don

lessons.lesson: Ideas from YouTube can be copied successfully with no experience.
